To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the asymptotic result for HQ holds for a class of models which includes the class of multivariable linear stochastic systems with non-Gaussian noise, and that the result can be proved using explicitly stated known techniques under conditions slightly stronger than those in Hannan and Deister.

the maximized quasi likelihood function is asymptotically equivalent to its expectation, which is a linear function of the parameters, plus a Gaussian random variable, and that the HQ criterion is asymptotically optimal.
the asymptotic result for multivariable, nonlinear systems is valid for the HQ criterion and that the HQ criterion can be extended to Hidden Markov Models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (i) How to prove that the HQ criterion can be applied to stochastic systems?
the derivation of a two-stage information criterion that is applicable to multivariable linear stochastic systems, with or without exogenous inputs.
the asymptotic analysis of a class of information criteria for model order selection in multivariable linear stochastic models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotics of HQ is correct for the class of multivariable, linear, stochastic systems considered by Hannan and Quinn.
HQ can be applied to the estimation of the orders of linear, multivariable, time series systems.
HQ is asymptotically optimal in the sense that it asymptotically minimizes the mean integrated squared error of the model selection procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HQ criterion is a good choice for model selection of multivariable, linear stochastic systems.
we have provided a new and transparent proof for the applicability of HQ, which is a first step for further research in the direction of model selection in stochastic systems with hidden variables.
the two-stage information criterion of HQ can be applied to a much broader class of models than originally thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of linear stochastic systems, HQ can be derived by a simple application of a result due to Akaike.
a simple, two-step argument, involving only the use of the Delta method, is enough to establish the asymptotic result for a large class of models.
the asymptotics of the HQ criterion can be derived in a straightforward manner by applying known techniques.
